program: Reality Replay — Phase 1G: Circadian Attention Validation
data_limitations: Only ~64 hours of operational data available — insufficient for full circadian confidence
System started mid-day (12:54 UTC), so early active hours are under-sampled on day 1
Only 2 real guardian reflex incidents observed, both during late_night period
Transition_morning has very low event counts (93) making statistical conclusions weak
No weekend data — all data falls on weekday (Monday–Wednesday)

quiet_hours.description: Low operator activity expected; autonomous operations dominate

late_night.description: Late-night autonomous cycles; both real incidents occurred here

quiet_hours.false_positive_analysis: 60% of flagged anomalies were REVIEW_REQUIRED that did not escalate to BLOCK — dominated by skillify pipeline test proposals during automated testing
notable_events: Skillify pipeline governance tests generated most REVIEW/BLOCK events
Autonomous DMN ticks continued without incidents

transition_morning.false_positive_analysis: No anomalies flagged during this period
notable_events: Very low activity — system in semantic consolidation phase
Dream replay and simulation occurred near this period

active_hours.false_positive_analysis: 71% false positive rate but absolute numbers are very low (10 out of 14 anomalies were test/development artifacts)
notable_events: Bootstrap and initial telemetry capture occurred here
Most governance framework tests ran during active hours
Test-driven anomalies (rm -rf /, destructive command tests) dominate BLOCK events

transition_evening.false_positive_analysis: Clean period with no anomalies detected
notable_events: Steady autonomous operation with no incidents

late_night.false_positive_analysis: 50% FP rate; however, this period contains both REAL incidents (memory pressure at 21:49 and 22:14 UTC) — the anomaly detection was justified
notable_events: CRITICAL: Both real memory-pressure incidents occurred at 21:49 and 22:14 UTC
Guardian reflex correctly triggered and escalated both times
Highest event density of any period (126.3/h) due to burst telemetry during incident
Health score dropped from 86.99 to 65.79 during first incident

anomaly_rate_ranking.note: Highest — but dominated by skillify test artifacts, not real anomalies
Real incidents occurred here; anomaly rate justified
Low anomaly rate; governance framework tests contribute
No anomalies; very low overall activity

key_findings: Real incidents cluster in late_night (21:00–00:00 UTC) — both memory pressure events occurred at 21:49 and 22:14
Quiet hours show high anomaly counts but these are dominated by automated test activity (skillify), not genuine anomalies
Active hours have low anomaly rates despite highest human activity — system is well-supervised
Transition periods (morning/evening) are the calmest — potential windows for reduced sensitivity
Late_night has the highest event throughput (126.3/h) driven by burst telemetry during incidents

quiet_hours.rationale: Reduce sensitivity slightly — high anomaly count is inflated by automated test artifacts; maintain reasonable baseline for genuine anomalies

specific_adjustments.skillify_pipeline: Apply 0.6x salience dampening to routine skillify rejections
specific_adjustments.somatic_anomalies: Maintain 1.0x — no reduction for somatic signals
specific_adjustments.governance_blocks: Maintain 1.0x — always attend to BLOCK-level events

transition_morning.rationale: Slightly increase sensitivity — very low activity means any signal is more novel and potentially important

specific_adjustments.novelty_boost: Increase novelty weight to 0.20 (from 0.15) during sparse periods

active_hours.rationale: Standard sensitivity — operator present, system well-supervised, no adjustment needed

transition_evening.rationale: No adjustment needed — clean operational record, standard sensitivity sufficient

late_night.rationale: INCREASE sensitivity — both real incidents occurred during this period; operator likely absent; autonomous responses must be more vigilant

specific_adjustments.temporal_decay_half_life: Extend to 120s (from 60s) to avoid losing track of slow-developing issues

circadian_policy_recommendation.summary: Implement time-aware salience adjustments: increase late_night sensitivity by 25% (where real incidents cluster), reduce quiet_hours by 15% (to dampen test artifacts), and boost transition_morning novelty detection by 10%.
circadian_policy_recommendation.confidence_rationale: Only 64 hours of data with 2 real incidents is insufficient for high-confidence circadian modeling. Recommendations are directionally correct but require validation with more operational history.
circadian_policy_recommendation.implementation_priority: MEDIUM — circadian adjustments should be deployed after accumulating at least 2 weeks of operational data
circadian_policy_recommendation.monitoring: Track false positive rates and missed escalations per period after implementing adjustments

score_breakdown.data_sufficiency_note: 64 hours covers ~2.7 full circadian cycles — minimum for pattern detection, insufficient for statistical confidence
score_breakdown.incident_coverage_note: Both real incidents were correctly detected and escalated during late_night; no missed escalations
score_breakdown.false_positive_management_note: High FP rate in quiet_hours (60%) and active_hours (71%) but dominated by test artifacts, not production false alarms
score_breakdown.period_differentiation_note: Clear differences between periods exist, but driven more by operational patterns (tests, development) than true circadian variation
score_breakdown.recommendation_actionability_note: Recommendations are reasonable but require more data to validate; late_night sensitivity increase is the strongest recommendation
